findings.title: Working-hours recheck rejects valid slots whenever a host has more than one window
findings.body: checkIfIsAvailable now runs for every isFixed host, and personal events, collective events, and round-robin fixed hosts are all marked isFixed. The new working-hours test uses Array.find and returns unavailable if the slot falls outside any single window whose days include the slot's UTC weekday. A host with a lunch break, or a single local range that getWorkingHours splits across UTC midnight into two entries on the same day, therefore fails the check for every slot: a 10:00 slot inside 09:00–12:00 is still outside 13:00–17:00, so find matches and the slot is dropped. The booking page then shows no times. The condition is also inverted for days off: if no window lists that weekday, find matches nothing and the host is treated as free, so a fixed host who does not work that day is not actually blocked. The end minute is copied from slot start (hour*60+minute of slotStartTime, not slot end), so a slot that starts inside a window but whose event length runs past endTime is accepted. Net effect is both false unavailability for ordinary split schedules and false availability outside hours.

findings.title: Date-override hit skips busy times and mishandles multiple or empty overrides
findings.body: On a day that has a date override, if the slot is considered inside an override, checkIfIsAvailable sets dateOverrideExist and returns true immediately, before the busy/booking loop. A fixed host (including every personal or collective host) who blocked 15:00 with a calendar event or Cal booking, but has a date override covering that time, is reported free, so the slot stays bookable and can double-book. The same find() treats "outside this one override" as a hard unavailable: two override windows on the same day reject a slot that sits in only one of them, because the other window's callback returns true. Zero-length overrides (the unavailable-day convention, start equal to end) are detected with dayjs object ===, which is never true for two instances, so that branch never runs. Day matching compares dayjs(date.start).add(offset).format (process-local mode) to slotStartTime.format (UTC mode), so when the server TZ is not UTC the override is attached to the wrong calendar day or ignored. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it is not treated as outside, so it takes the early available return as well.

findings.title: Override timezone shift uses Date.toString and drops times that cross midnight
findings.body: Active date overrides are converted with dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone). Date.toString() is the process-local representation (and often includes a parenthetical zone name), so the parsed instant used for utcOffset is wrong or Invalid Date off UTC, and utcOffset becomes NaN. timeZone is optional on TimeRange; if it is missing, .tz(undefined) throws RangeError and getSlots fails for the whole day instead of falling back. The shifted clock time is then reduced with .hour() and .minute() only. Adding inviteeOffset-organizerOffset across midnight wraps to 0–24h on the unadjusted day (the activeOverrides filter still keys off the raw UTC start). When the wrapped end is less than the wrapped start, buildSlots drops the range (start >= end), so the override disappears. Attendees in a distant timezone see the override on the wrong date or not at all — the bug this change is meant to fix.

findings.title: No test covers fixed-host overrides or the new availability recheck
findings.body: The only new test re-queries a personal event date override in Asia/Dhaka and expects the same UTC instants as the IST case. It never builds a round-robin event with a fixed host, which is the main fix described in the PR, and it never hits checkIfIsAvailable's date-override or working-hours branches. Split working hours, an override day that also has a booking, an unavailable (start==end) override, and a timezone shift that crosses midnight are all untested, so the regressions above would merge green.
